I'm another nomad from the Great Migration, so I'm a tad lost at the moment. This morning was the first time the site loaded up smoothly for me, so I'll hopefully be able to get a better look around. I honestly haven't been able to look through any other /v/introductions threads, so I'm not sure what I'm even supposed to put here. I'll treat it like any other forum then.

I'm in my mid-20s, male, and at the point in my life where I'm trying to recognize the difference between the things I find interesting and the things I can and want to spend my time on. The hallmarks of my hobbies that haven't faded are:

  • Classic cars: over the course of about 10 years, I rebuilt a car together with my dad. The only way I'll not have that car is if someone crashes it or steals it.
  • Motorcycles: again, lots of time spent in the garage with dad and my brothers
  • Computers: I may have grown up a gearhead, but it really was because I love to tinker. Computers were great for that, and Linux only made it better. I'm dual-booting Mint 17.1/ Win7 and brute force learning Dvorak at the moment. Typing this post has taken far longer than I would like to admit.
  • Formula 1: I've always love F1, and in the past couple of years I have gotten to where I regularly follow it.
  • Stereos and Music: My wife and I recently had her heirloom tube console stereo rebuilt, so analog sound is a growing interest of ours. I've got the bug to go big and build a nice Hi-fi setup for the living room, but alas no time for now.
  • Gaming: I almost hesitate to put this on here, simply for lack of time more than lack of interest. I'm currently trying to catch up on the big titles in gaming from the last couple years, and split my time into Elite:Dangerous as well.
  • Bodyweight fitness: Got back into the routine of exercise really recently (past month or two) and my gymnastics roots appealed to me more than wanting to go lift weights.

That's probably a good enough chunk to put in here. It's not an exhaustive list of interest by any means, but I would list those as my top interests right now.

Thanks for reading, I'll see the lot of you around.

What exactly is wrong with chrome UI?

Just to start with, I absolutely hate the refusal to recognize the arbitrary nature of putting the tabs on top rather than on bottom; making crap up about conceptualizations won't change that. A simple option to restore the old style isn't too much to ask for(which brings up another issue I have with it: having fewer options than programs from the goddamn nineties; Gnome's "options kill kittens" philosophy isn't one that should be emulated).

Second, there's absolutely no way to bring the controls to the fore(tying in somewhat to the lack of customizability); beyond the basic ones, everything's hidden behind a single settings menu that add an extra click and more mouse movement that necessary over an old-fashioned menubar.

Third, the lack of a status bar; little tooltips that fade away after a few moments are simply no replacement for having that information available persistently.

Internet Explorer does the minimalistic interface right: it's there by default, can be added to and the full menu bar is simply a keystroke away(even if it can't be put in its traditional position).
